definition: Regulation, supervision or a mandatory standard is presented as a reason for action or reporting.
include_when: The document links a process, investment, data collection or report to CSRD, ESRS, Taxonomy, banking or sector regulation.
exclude_when: Regulation appears only in a glossary or generic context.
example: CSRD readiness caused a new data-control process.

definition: Investor, lender, customer or market expectation influences the agenda.
include_when: A stakeholder demand is linked to target selection, product, financing, rating or disclosure.
exclude_when: A stakeholder list is provided without influence.
example: Investor attention influenced KPI design.

definition: Parent group, owner or controlling shareholder shapes a policy, target or reporting boundary.
include_when: The report attributes a commitment, target or reset to group governance.
exclude_when: The group is mentioned only in company description.
example: Goals were reset after separation from a former group framework.

definition: Action is justified by cost, resilience, safety, reliability, efficiency or core operational performance.
include_when: The report connects ESG action to operating performance or continuity.
exclude_when: Only moral or reputational language is used.
example: Energy efficiency is used in server-upgrade decisions.

definition: Action or disclosure is linked to trust, reputation, public acceptance or stakeholder confidence.
include_when: The report explicitly frames transparency, rating or social licence as a benefit.
exclude_when: Public communication alone is not sufficient.
example: A separate report is retained for accessibility to stakeholders.

definition: A process identifies impact materiality and financial materiality.
include_when: Methods, thresholds, stakeholders, value-chain boundaries or validation are described.
exclude_when: The words double materiality appear without process detail.
example: Management validates material IROs after scoring.

definition: A material topic is connected to how the company creates value or to its core product or service.
include_when: The report explains why the topic matters to the sector or business model.
exclude_when: A topic is merely listed as material.
example: Financed emissions are linked to the lending portfolio.

definition: Stakeholder engagement informs materiality, strategy or priorities.
include_when: The stakeholder group, engagement channel and use of input are identified.
exclude_when: A stakeholder list has no described influence.
example: A trade union regularly discusses the social strategy.

definition: A board or supervisory body has an explicit sustainability oversight role.
include_when: Responsibility, reporting cadence, approval or evaluation is stated.
exclude_when: Board members are merely named.
example: An ESG status report is presented to the board twice a year.

definition: A named function or executive owns the ESG agenda.
include_when: Role and authority are described.
exclude_when: A spokesperson is quoted without responsibility.
example: A board member performs the Chief Sustainability Officer role.

definition: A dedicated ESG or sustainability committee coordinates or oversees decisions.
include_when: Membership, mandate, cadence or correction power is provided.
exclude_when: A committee is named without any role.
example: A CEO-chaired committee reviews targets quarterly.

definition: The organisation specifies how often performance or risks are reviewed.
include_when: A recurring review is linked to a body or KPI.
exclude_when: A one-off meeting with no recurring process.
example: Strategic KPIs are evaluated quarterly.

definition: Controls, lines of defence, audit, due diligence or corrective action are described.
include_when: The mechanism can verify, escalate or change action.
exclude_when: A general promise to comply.
example: Risk and compliance functions form additional lines of defence.

definition: The report describes sustainability expertise, training or external advice used by governance bodies.
include_when: Expertise is tied to ability to oversee or decide.
exclude_when: General employee awareness only.
example: An external sustainability council advises the board.

definition: Sustainability affects an investment plan or capital expenditure.
include_when: A target, taxonomy assessment or transition plan is linked to CapEx approval or portfolio allocation.
exclude_when: Green projects are listed without an allocation mechanism.
example: A transition plan is approved through the investment plan.

definition: Sustainability affects an operating budget or recurring resource allocation.
include_when: OpEx is assigned or classified with a decision mechanism.
exclude_when: A one-off donation has no governance link.
example: Taxonomy-aligned OpEx is used in company decisions.

definition: ESG information changes risk identification, limits, pricing, underwriting or mitigation.
include_when: A risk process, matrix, control or decision rule is described.
exclude_when: Risk is mentioned generically.
example: Climate data enter underwriting or collateral valuation.

definition: ESG performance affects variable compensation or evaluation.
include_when: A KPI, weight, target or assessment process is stated.
exclude_when: Remuneration is described without an ESG link.
example: Board ESG KPIs materially affect variable remuneration.

definition: ESG shapes a product, service or financed portfolio.
include_when: Design, eligibility, exclusion, target or portfolio shift is described.
exclude_when: A product is called sustainable without criteria.
example: Low-emission vehicle development covers the product life cycle.

definition: ESG criteria affect supplier selection, monitoring or purchasing.
include_when: Rating, audit, due diligence, corrective action or procurement condition is used.
exclude_when: A supplier code exists without evidence of application.
example: Strategic suppliers are subject to a sustainability rating target.

definition: ESG metrics influence operations, maintenance or process design.
include_when: The report links a metric to a concrete recurring operational choice.
exclude_when: An activity is described without a decision mechanism.
example: Energy efficiency affects data-centre upgrade selection.

definition: A metric has a baseline, target value and target year.
include_when: At least a comparable base and time-bound target are stated.
exclude_when: An aspiration lacks a baseline or date.
example: Emission intensity is to decline by 2030 from a 2019 baseline.

definition: Comparable values are shown across multiple periods.
include_when: At least two periods use a sufficiently explained boundary.
exclude_when: A single current value is shown.
example: Scope 1–3 values are shown for 2022–2024.

definition: The organisational or methodological boundary is explained.
include_when: Entities, scopes, calculation method, exclusions or restatement are stated.
exclude_when: A metric label is provided without method or scope.
example: Historical values were recalculated after a methodology change.

definition: A metric records activity or immediate output rather than downstream change.
include_when: Counts of participants, projects, suppliers, training or funds are reported.
exclude_when: A validated change in condition or behaviour is measured.
example: Number of people trained in digital literacy.

definition: A metric records a change in operational, social or environmental condition.
include_when: Reduction, rate, intensity or measured change is stated.
exclude_when: Input or activity count only.
example: Water use per manufactured vehicle declined from the baseline.

definition: The document attributes a broader societal or environmental effect to an action.
include_when: Causal or contribution language about downstream impact is used.
exclude_when: An operational output is reported with no broader attribution.
example: A programme is said to improve community quality of life.

definition: The report explicitly describes a material actual or potential adverse impact.
include_when: A negative effect, affected group, horizon or persistence is described.
exclude_when: A generic risk disclaimer.
example: Coal mining is described as having a permanent biodiversity impact.

definition: A disclosed KPI worsens or moves away from target.
include_when: The current value is less favourable than a comparable prior value or target.
exclude_when: No comparator is available.
example: Scope 1+2 emissions increase year on year.

definition: The report admits a missing target, incomplete data or unavailable information.
include_when: A limitation is explicit.
exclude_when: The analyst merely infers that detail is missing.
example: No outcome target exists for financed emissions.

definition: A target, boundary or method is reset, cancelled, expanded or restated.
include_when: The reason or affected metric is identifiable.
exclude_when: A routine update has no comparability effect.
example: Historical carbon data are restated after a method change.

definition: Competing objectives or costs are acknowledged.
include_when: The document discusses competitiveness, affordability, reliability or transition costs against ESG aims.
exclude_when: A generic claim that sustainability creates value.
example: ESG ambition is explicitly balanced against competitiveness.

definition: An independent practitioner provides limited assurance over specified disclosures.
include_when: Scope and assurance standard are identifiable.
exclude_when: Internal audit, certification or an award.
example: ISAE 3000 limited assurance over a sustainability statement.

definition: An independent practitioner provides reasonable assurance over a specified metric, method or disclosure.
include_when: The report explicitly states reasonable assurance and its scope.
exclude_when: Limited assurance or internal verification.
example: A defined financed-emissions calculation receives reasonable assurance.

definition: The organisation explicitly states that the report was not externally assured.
include_when: A non-assurance statement is present.
exclude_when: No assurance report is visible but absence is not stated.
example: The ESG report states that it was not externally assured.

definition: The statement is attributed to the reporting organisation and was not independently verified by this study.
include_when: Narrative claims, commitments and company interpretations.
exclude_when: A legal fact from primary law or a result independently verified within scope.
example: The company states that a programme created positive change.

definition: The segment reports a numerical measure or target produced by the organisation.
include_when: A defined value, time series, baseline or target is presented.
exclude_when: Pure narrative with no measurable value.
example: Adjusted pay gap changed from one year to the next.

definition: The organisation explicitly acknowledges a gap, uncertainty, adverse trend or missing element.
include_when: The limitation is stated in the source.
exclude_when: The analyst infers silence.
example: No outcome target has yet been established.

definition: Meaning is constructed by the analyst rather than directly stated.
include_when: A cross-case pattern, typology or inferred relationship is proposed.
exclude_when: A neutral paraphrase of the source.
example: Decision integration is stronger where targets enter capital allocation.

definition: A value statement or strategic commitment is made without a concrete mechanism.
include_when: No owner, activity, metric or decision link is provided.
exclude_when: A concrete project or target is reported.
example: Sustainability is a strategic priority.

definition: A specific action or output is disclosed, while management mechanism or outcome remains weak.
include_when: A project, training count, supplier engagement or donation is reported.
exclude_when: A time-bound managed result or decision link is explicit.
example: Two hundred suppliers were engaged.

definition: A target, owner, process, method, boundary, time series or correction is sufficiently specified.
include_when: At least one formal management or comparable-result mechanism is visible.
exclude_when: A direct allocation, risk, product, supplier, remuneration or operational decision link is explicit.
example: A metric has a baseline, target year and annual progress.

definition: Sustainability information demonstrably enters allocation, risk, product, procurement, remuneration or operational choice.
include_when: A formal decision consequence or rule is explicit.
exclude_when: A strategic priority, committee or assured report exists without a decision link.
example: An ESG KPI affects variable remuneration.

definition: A specifically bounded result or calculation has a clear method and strong independent support through assurance or triangulation.
include_when: The external support covers the exact result and the claim stays within that scope.
exclude_when: General report assurance, a decision link without verification, or an untested causal impact claim.
example: A defined financed-emissions calculation is subject to reasonable assurance.
